best_for: API developers and testers who want a desktop client for building, testing and documenting requests, solo for free or shared with a team on a paid plan.
description:
Postman is an API platform from Postman, Inc., and this desktop app is where you build and run requests against an API. Postman says more than 50 million developers and 500,000 companies use it.

The Postman CLI installs from npm and runs your collections and tests from a terminal, for example on every commit in your build pipeline. A Postman plugin for coding agents such as Claude, OpenAI's tools and Cursor loads skills that create collections with tests, spin up mock servers before an API exists, and simulate heavy load. The Postman API Network lets you browse public APIs from companies in payments, travel, e-commerce and more.

points.title: Use it without an account
points.text: When you are not signed in, the desktop app opens a lightweight API client. You can build and send requests, keep a history and run post-response scripts. That work stays on your machine and is not synced.

points.title: Signing in moves you to workspaces
points.text: Collections, environments, mock servers, monitors and sharing live in workspaces, which need a free Postman account. You can move open requests and history from the lightweight client when you sign in.

points.title: Free covers one person
points.text: The Free plan includes the API client, collections, specs, mock servers, the collection runner and Git integration, for a single user. Solo, also for one user, is USD 9 per month billed yearly and adds data-driven testing and more monitoring.

points.title: Teams pay per seat
points.text: Team is USD 19 per user per month billed yearly and adds collaboration and role-based access. Enterprise is priced by sales. Paying yearly instead of monthly saves up to 25 percent. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: AI is metered
points.text: Each plan includes a monthly allowance of AI credits, with overage billed per credit. Cloud performance testing is billed per virtual-user hour.

points.title: Builds for Intel and Arm
points.text: Postman ships for Windows, macOS and Linux on both x64 and Arm64. On Linux it needs the libX11-xcb library, which minimal and server installs may lack. The Flatpak listed here is a Flathub build that Flathub does not mark as verified.

points.title: History is a Windows thing
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 401 versions, with a per-user installer. macOS (Intel and Apple silicon) and Linux list only the current release, so older builds there need another source.
